column1: # One owner per type, and the twins that survive on purpose.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   name              the declared name; an optional kind prefix says what it is
#                       (no prefix) a type: class, struct, union, enum, alias
#                       func:       a function
#                       dup:        a whole-file duplicate group, read by
#                                   dup-scan.py and skipped by this gate
#   canonical         where the name is declared, relative to the workspace root
#                       (the parent directory holding the side-by-side clones)
#   mirrors           comma-separated sanctioned second sites, or - for none
# Every sanctioned mirror also carries, at the declaration itself:
#     // MIRROR-OF: <canonical path> - <reason>
# so a reader who lands on the mirror learns it is one without leaving the file.
# An unregistered second declaration is a build error; a registered one is a
# decision on the record, with its reason next to it.
# A canonical site that stops declaring its own name fails too. That is the
# shape a careless fix to this gate produces, so it is named rather than
# assumed impossible.
# --- the sealed public carrier and the working buffer are NOT the same concept.
# One is a value type a consumer receives across the published surface and may
# not resize; the other is the scratch a card read fills in place and wipes.
# Collapsing them would hand a caller a buffer it can grow.
Buffer
SecureBuffer
# --- the sdbus-c++ bus peer and the Qt fake are two fakes of one agent, and
# they cannot be one file: the PKCS#11 module's test tree may not link Qt.
FakeAgent
# --- the ICAO 9303 4.9 check digit, three times, three error policies:
# the middleware throws, the agent returns -1 without ever materialising the
# secret bytes as a std::string, the prompter walks QChar. Unifying them costs
# a new public middleware API to save forty lines. The golden vectors pin them
# instead, one table asserted from all three packages.
func:computeCheckDigit
func:checkDigitVerifies
func:mrzCheckDigit
func:checkDigitOk
# --- the public signing vocabulary and the engine's own. The bridge between
# them is a translation, not an accident: the published enum may not move when
# the engine's does.
SignatureFormat
SignatureLevel
# --- the wire vocabulary has four mirrors on purpose: the core enum, the Qt
# client's, the Swift client's, and the CDDL the three are checked against.
# A parity test already pins them; this row is so nobody "fixes" them.
SyncError
# --- the four helpers the desktop plugins each had their own copy of. The
# lookups they call already lived in one header, so the bodies moved next to
# their own callees.
func:photoBytes
func:firstFieldBytes
LabelledField
func:securityStatusText
# --- the per-operation stall bound the two live controllers arm. Its second
# copy carried a comment arguing that two arming sites did not justify a shared
# helper; the copy dragged the card-gone sentence with it, which that comment
# did not price.
OpWatch
func:armWatchdog
func:cardGoneText
# --- the two verdict vocabularies five flows and two seams each declared for
# themselves. Identical enumerators, identical order, identical meaning; the
# flows now alias the one definition, so their own spellings stay at the call
# sites and the type has an owner.
FlowOutcome
SeamStatus
# --- the annex reading order, the one user-visible thing this collapse moves.
# Both desktop hosts kept a hand-written, byte-identical list of the same
# fifteen keys, each pinned by its own test, each asking the reader to change
# both together. The KDE host keeps its own name for the call, which is what
# makes its pin a second independent failure when the shared order moves.
func:fieldOrderForGroup
# --- the two-shape card-date rule. Only the PARSING half is shared: what a
# host shows for a value that is not a date has a catalogue behind it and stays
# in the host, which is why the library returns nothing rather than a word.
func:normalizedCardDate
# --- the security vocabulary. The middleware's copy is the PRODUCER's, in a
# published plugin surface a card plugin writes against: it may not move, and
# the client's is the reader of the same tokens. The desktop host re-exports
# the name into its own namespace so its call sites are unchanged. A parity
# test holds the producer's token set against the reader's.
SecurityCategory
SecurityCheckStatus
func:statusFromString
func:categoryFromString
# --- vendored OASIS PKCS#11 headers, twice. The Qt-free module may not reach
# across into the middleware for them, so the copy stays and is pinned instead.
# The second copy now ships from the agent, not from the platform host: the
# module that consumes it is built there. No MIRROR-OF marker on either side --
# annotating a third party's source is editing it.
dup:oasis-pkcs11t
dup:oasis-pkcs11f
dup:oasis-pkcs11
# --- two vendored builds of one third-party library for two platforms. Most of
# their headers coincide and a few legitimately do not, so this row says the
# trees are allowed to coincide and claims nothing about which files do. No
# marker is added to either: annotating a third party's source is editing it.
dup:vendored-openssl
